label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, money-unit, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 10 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy payments-api: PROVIDER_BREAKER on (unchanged), CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT dollars -> cents, REFUND_CONNECTION returned (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: money-unit
case.title: Customers charged 100 times the amount: a money-unit bug
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the payments API with a money-unit bug (CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars): it reads each payment's amount, already in cents, as dollars and converts it to cents again, so the provider charges every customer 100 times the amount, while our own records keep the right one.
case.remedy: roll the payments API back to CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents, then refund each customer charged since the deploy what was charged above the amount, at the provider: our API refunds no more than our recorded amount (a write, so it needs approval)

expected_symptoms: the money check fails on payments_match_provider, at the first evaluation after the deploy: for each payment since, the provider charged 100 times our amount ('amount differs')
the ledger books what the provider charged, so it agrees with the provider, and the other invariants pass
the payment confirmer logs a conflict for each such payment: the provider charged a different amount than our payment's

a payment whose answer was lost during the fault stays pending for good ('pending but charged, amount differs'): the confirmer refuses the provider's 100 times amount; its client's retries raise the p95 of POST /payments to about 0.6 s, under its threshold
the API stays healthy, and its answers show the right amount
refunds send the right amount: a full refund gives back 1% of what was charged
fault.remedy: roll the payments API back to CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents, then refund each customer charged since the deploy what was charged above the amount, at the provider: our API refunds no more than our recorded amount (a write, so it needs approval)

diagnosis.hypothesis:
payments-api was redeployed at 19:07:06Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. Since then it sends the provider amounts 100x what it records. Our payments table stores cents correctly (pmt_000245: 1396), but the provider charged 139600 cents (pay_000245). So payments_match_provider reports 'amount differs' for each new payment from pmt_000245, the first payment logged after the deploy (19:07:07.6Z). Findings grew from 59 at the alert to 92 at c1's cutoff, so the damage is ongoing.

The ledger books from provider webhooks, so it agrees with the provider at the inflated amounts, and ledger_balanced and matches_provider pass. Customers are overcharged 100x. Refunds went out in our cents amounts (1396 back on a 139600 charge), so refunded customers are still out the difference.

The exact conversion is inferred from the 100x ratio. The trace does not show the request body, and nothing shows the setting's previous value.

evidence.shows: Only payments_match_provider fails, with evidence_total 92. The 5 findings shown all say 'amount differs', each with the provider charge exactly 100x our amount_cents (1396→139600, 12165→1216500, ...). The summary starts at pmt_000245. The ledger is balanced and matches the provider at $507,186.08. Refunds agree. Only 5 of the 92 findings are shown in full.
payments-api is the only service recreated after the 19:05:39Z stack start. It was recreated at 19:07:06Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. All other services were unchanged since 19:05:39Z.
pmt_000245 succeeded at 19:07:07.619Z with amount_cents 1396 and provider_payment_id pay_000245. It was later refunded only 1396 (rfd_000024).
pmt_000245's request inserted our amount_cents and POSTed to fake-provider /v1/payments, which returned 200. The request body, and so the amount sent, is not recorded.
pmt_000244 (1359 cents) succeeded at 19:07:06.448Z, at the deploy boundary. Findings start at pmt_000245, consistent with the error beginning with the new container.

proposed_fix.summary:
Roll payments-api back to its pre-19:07:06Z settings, which restores the prior CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT, so new charges go out in the correct amount. Then rerun the money check and confirm no new findings appear after the rollback.

As a separate, human-led data repair: for each affected payment (pmt_000245 onward, 92+ so far), refund the overcharged difference at the provider, including those already partly refunded such as pmt_000245/rfd_000024. Then confirm the ledger follows the provider's refund webhooks.

diagnosis.blast_radius:
The payments-api container is recreated, so payment and refund requests fail or wait during the restart. Clients retrying with idempotency keys should be safe.

If the prior setting was also wrong, or something else changed, the rollback may not stop the mismatch. The rerun of the money check will show that.

The rollback repairs nothing. The overcharges already at the provider, and the ledger entries booked at inflated amounts, stay until a data repair.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy payments-api with the settings from the 19:07:06Z deploy (CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars, PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, REFUND_CONNECTION=returned). This is not advisable unless the rollback itself breaks payments, since those settings are what cause the overcharges.
